your_challenge: Study one real motion system then create your own: named eases (CustomEase) + duration tokens + 5 registered effects. Refactor 3 earlier demos to use only your tokens
react_how: Export tokens from one module; register effects once in your shared gsap file
done_when: No hardcoded duration/ease left in the refactored demos
look_up_these: motion tokens; productive vs expressive motion; registerEffect
watch_out_for: Every component inventing its own timings

what_it_does: How transforms combine; where they pivot; why z-index sometimes stops working
real_world_use_case: Debugging elements hiding behind others during animation
your_challenge: Build a demo where a transformed parent traps a child z-index (a dropdown hidden behind the next card). Fix it in two different ways and understand why each works
react_how: Plain JSX + CSS modules or Tailwind; no GSAP needed for the bug itself
done_when: You can predict when a new stacking context is created
look_up_these: stacking context triggers (transform / opacity / filter / position+z-index); transform order
watch_out_for: Animating opacity or transform creating a new stacking context mid-animation

what_it_does: Hiding content outside a box so it can slide in from nowhere
real_world_use_case: Line reveals; image reveals; text roll hovers
your_challenge: Build 3 reveals with no plugins: text sliding up from behind an invisible edge; an image wiping in; a button label rolling. Use only overflow/clip-path wrappers + GSAP y/yPercent
react_how: Make a reusable <Mask> wrapper component
done_when: No content visible outside the mask at any frame
look_up_these: overflow: hidden; overflow: clip; clip-path inset; wrapper elements
watch_out_for: Putting overflow on the element you animate instead of its parent

what_it_does: Native sticky vs JS pinning: when each is the right choice
real_world_use_case: Sticky headers; side navs; scroll stories
your_challenge: Build the same pinned section twice: CSS sticky only and ScrollTrigger pin. List what sticky cannot do (scrubbed timeline while stuck; pin spacing; horizontal) and when sticky is better (simpler; no JS)
react_how: Same component with a prop to switch implementation
done_when: You choose correctly between them in later builds
look_up_these: position: sticky; sticky + overflow parent bug; pinSpacing
watch_out_for: Sticky silently failing because an ancestor has overflow hidden

what_it_does: Blending layers (difference / multiply / screen) and filters (blur / grayscale)
real_world_use_case: Inverting cursors; text that inverts over images; blur transitions
your_challenge: Make a big cursor circle that inverts the text under it (difference) and a page transition that blurs out and in. Measure the blur performance cost
react_how: Blend layer as a fixed component in the root layout
done_when: Cursor inverts correctly over light and dark areas; blur stays smooth
look_up_these: mix-blend-mode: difference; isolation; filter: blur; backdrop-filter
watch_out_for: Large animated blur = expensive; isolation needed to contain blending

what_it_does: What the browser can now do without GSAP (transitions / keyframes / animation-timeline: scroll())
your_challenge: Build a scroll progress bar and a reveal-on-scroll using ONLY CSS scroll-driven animations. Then list 3 things you could not do without GSAP
react_how: Pure CSS in a component; compare with your GSAP version side by side
done_when: You can justify GSAP vs native CSS for any effect
look_up_these: transition; @keyframes; animation-timeline; view(); scroll(); browser support
watch_out_for: Using native scroll timelines without checking browser support

what_it_does: Turn a designer video/prototype into exact timings and eases
your_challenge: Find a motion shot on Dribbble; step through it frame by frame; write down every element / start time / duration / ease BEFORE coding; then build it and compare side by side
react_how: Each shot becomes one component; timings in a spec object at the top of the file
done_when: Side-by-side recording looks near identical; your written spec matched what you built
look_up_these: frame-by-frame; storyboard; timing sheet; CustomEase from curves
watch_out_for: Coding by eye without a timing plan

topic: GSAP vs Motion (Framer Motion) vs CSS
what_it_does: Know the trade-offs between the main React animation options
real_world_use_case: Interview question; choosing tools on the job
your_challenge: Build the SAME component (staggered list + layout change + exit animation + scroll reveal) three times: GSAP / Motion for React / pure CSS. Compare bundle size; code length; control; what each struggles with
react_how: Three sibling components on one page with identical behavior
done_when: You can argue for each tool in a specific situation with evidence from your build
look_up_these: motion.dev React; AnimatePresence; layout animations; bundle size
watch_out_for: Picking one tool for everything without knowing the trade-offs

what_it_does: Show HOW you built each project, not just the result
real_world_use_case: What hiring managers read; makes your work interview-ready
your_challenge: For each Build write a case-study page in your portfolio: the goal; a breakdown GIF/video of 3 key effects; the technique behind each; one hard bug and how you solved it (your error_log is the source); performance numbers
react_how: Case studies are MDX or React pages in your portfolio app
done_when: Each build has a published case study with real perf numbers
look_up_these: case study structure; Lighthouse; screen recording
watch_out_for: Showing only the pretty result with no reasoning
